reference.title: An absolute sodium abundance for a cloud-free 'hot Saturn' exoplanet

detections.abstract_quote: Here we present an optical transmission spectrum for the 'hot-Saturn' WASP-96b obtained with the Very Large Telescope, which exhibits the complete pressure-broadened profile of the sodium absorption feature.

reference.title: Awesome SOSS: atmospheric characterization of WASP-96 b using the JWST early release observations

detections.abstract_quote: We constrain the logarithmic volume mixing ratios of multiple chemical species in its atmosphere, including: H2O = -3.59 +0.35/-0.35, CO2 = -4.38 +0.47/-0.57 and K = -8.04 +1.22/-1.71.

reference.title: Awesome SOSS: atmospheric characterization of WASP-96 b using the JWST early release observations

detections.note: Marked tentative by curator judgement: the abstract reports bounded abundance constraints ('We constrain the logarithmic volume mixing ratios') and gives no detection significance. The companion analysis of the same NIRISS/SOSS data, Radica et al. 2023, 'Awesome SOSS: transmission spectroscopy of WASP-96b with NIRISS/SOSS' (MNRAS 524, 835; doi:10.1093/mnras/stad1762), reports only metallicity/C/O constraints in its abstract and claims no individual species.

reference.title: Awesome SOSS: atmospheric characterization of WASP-96 b using the JWST early release observations

detections.note: Marked tentative by curator judgement: the abstract reports bounded abundance constraints ('We constrain the logarithmic volume mixing ratios') and gives no detection significance. The companion analysis of the same NIRISS/SOSS data, Radica et al. 2023, 'Awesome SOSS: transmission spectroscopy of WASP-96b with NIRISS/SOSS' (MNRAS 524, 835; doi:10.1093/mnras/stad1762), reports only metallicity/C/O constraints in its abstract and claims no individual species.
detections.abstract_quote: Notably, our results offer a first abundance constraint on potassium in WASP-96 b's atmosphere, and important inferences on carbon-bearing species such as CO2 and CO.

detections_note: Radica et al. 2023 (MNRAS 524, 835; doi:10.1093/mnras/stad1762; arXiv:2305.17001) is not listed as a detection. Its abstract gives only metallicity (1-5x solar) and solar C/O, plus a short-wavelength slope that 'could either be caused by enhanced Rayleigh scattering or the red wing of a pressure-broadened Na feature'.
